    AI Overview
    The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026, roughly 40 to 50 miles off the coast of San Diego, California, to safely conclude its 10-day mission. The spacecraft landed within one mile of its targeted recovery zone, where the USS John P. Murtha was waiting. 
    Key Landing Details: 
    • Location: Pacific Ocean, approximately 40–50 miles southwest of San Diego.
    • Time: 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
    • Targeting: The capsule landed with high precision, within one mile of the target area, according to CNN.
    • Recovery: The crew was retrieved by U.S. Navy vessels waiting in the area. 
    The landing followed a precise reentry maneuver to transition from its lunar trajectory to a targeted splashdown site off the California coast.

    How far from Earth will Artemis II go?
    Its farthest distance from Earth was 252,756 miles (406,771 km; 219,639 nmi) at 23:02 UTC, and it surpassed Apollo 13's 248,655 miles (400,171 km; 216,075 nmi) record as the farthest crewed mission from Earth at 17:56 UTC.
